2015_078_041415mtg.paragraph: Regular meeting agenda packet of the Troy School District Board of Education for April 14, 2015, convening at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Two 2014 Capital Projects Fund awards come before the Board: $308,486.00 across five bid categories for remodeling at Smith Middle School and Niles School, and $469,750.00 to EMC/Presidio for a bundled data storage and backup solution bought off the Western States Contracting Alliance contract. The packet also carries the February 2015 Treasurer's Report, showing total disbursements in the period of $5,761,924.73, and enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of STANFRED Consultants.

**Meeting** — Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, April 14, 2015, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition** — Mission Moment for Calen Knight, a Smith Middle School sixth grader who founded Calen4kids.org; Outstanding Teacher awards, with sixteen nominated, thirteen honored, and Katie Held (Troy Union), Charlie Tull (Larson) and Jane Moss (Athens) forwarded to Oakland Schools, Moss also named District overall Teacher of the Year with a free one-year car lease donated by the Suburban Collection; and Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence mini-grant recipients presented by president Al Robinson.

**Consent agenda** — February 24, 2015 special meeting minutes, where Resolutions 15-022, 15-023 and 15-024 each carried Yes 7 / No 0, giving Ms. Stephanie Maynard a two-year probationary contract as Director of Finance effective February 25, 2015, authorizing an owner's representative contract with Lecole Planners, and awarding interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools to Signature Specialty Coatings for $84,000.00; March 3, 2015 meeting minutes; March 17, 2015 workshop minutes; and the February 2015 Treasurer's Report.

**Curriculum reports** — Enrollment Projections, presented by Dr. Machesky from analysis by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of STANFRED Consultants, excluding 235 ECP, SCSE and GROW students; Schools of Choice enrollment rose from 287 in Fall 2009/10 to 907 in Fall 2014/15, and K-12 head count reached 12,309 in 2014/15, with 2019/20 projections of 13,102 high, 12,387 most likely and 11,674 low. **Other** — A Barton Malow update on the 2013 Bond Program Series 1; first readings of B-1210 Closed Session, B-1301 Agenda Format, B-1401 Minutes and J-2012 Anti-Bullying Policy; second readings and adoption of B-0102 Term of Office, B-1202 Place of Meeting, B-1204 Quorum and B-1211 Public Participation.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held April 14, 2015 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices are at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** The TSD Mission Moment honors Calen Knight, a sixth grade student at Smith Middle School, who at age seven donated stuffed animals and toys to children at Lighthouse of Oakland County and later founded her own charity, Calen4kids.org. Sixteen individuals were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award Program and thirteen honored: Erica Bachman (Wattles), Nadeen Brown (Leonard), Adam Burns (Athens High School), Karen Bush (Schroeder), Jason Cichowicz (Schroeder), Jennifer DeWard (Leonard), Lora Herbert (Hill), Sara Jozefiak (Barnard), Alan MacNair (Troy High School), Grayson McKinney (Costello), Debbie Motherwell (Martell), Kristy Pierce (Athens High School) and Amy Wallace (Leonard). Three chosen by a TEA selection committee went to Oakland Schools: Katie Held, kindergarten, Troy Union Elementary; Charlie Tull, math and technology, Larson Middle School; and Jane Moss, chemistry, Athens High School. Moss was also selected District overall Teacher of the Year and awarded a free one-year lease of a car donated by the Suburban Collection. Al Robinson, president of the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, recognizes recipients from the 81 mini-grants funded this year.

**February 24, 2015 special meeting minutes.** Held at the Administration Building; President Philippart convened at 5:30 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, plus Superintendent Machesky, Mark Dziatczak, Mary Haezebrouck, Larry Lobert and Rick West. Resolution 15-022 issued Ms. Stephanie Maynard a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Finance effective February 25, 2015 (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 15-023 authorized a contract with Lecole Planners for owner's representative services over capital projects associated with the 2014 bond issue (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 15-024 awarded interior painting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools to Signature Specialty Coatings for $84,000.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund (Yes 7, No 0). Minutes are submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**March 3, 2015 regular meeting minutes.** Vice President Schmidt convened at 7:01 p.m. before approximately 175 audience members; Philippart and Edmunds were absent and every roll call recorded Yes 5, No 0. Resolution 15-025 recognized February as Principal Appreciation Month; 15-026 approved the consent agenda; 15-027 closed Bemis, Schroeder, Athens High and Troy High to open enrollment for 2015/2016, excepting not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area and siblings in grades 9-11. Resolution 15-028 amended the 2014-15 General Fund budget, moving total revenues and incoming transfers from $131,253,100 to $142,706,181 and appropriating $143,627,633, against approved expenditures of $132,525,180, with an ending fund balance June 30 of $20,458,563 versus $18,040,548 approved. Resolution 15-029 awarded Athens High School central HVAC to ThermalNetics for $382,000.00, air/air energy recovery to Thermalnetics for $164,000.00 and secondary unit substitutions to Madison/Schneider Electric for $240,265.00; 15-030 awarded chiller equipment for Boulan Park, Larson and Athens to ThermalNetics, distributor for Daikin/McQuay, for $420,800.00. Mrs. Shawna Veit reported on the Oakland County Center Program Redesign and Ron Curtis of Barton Malow gave a bond update. The March 17, 2015 workshop was held at the Troy Center for Transition, 1291 Torpey, Troy, MI 48083, convening at 6:00 p.m. with Schmidt absent and adjourning at 9:24 p.m.

**Item 7.A, Enrollment Projections.** Dr. Machesky presents analysis by Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., of STANFRED Consultants. Head counts exclude 235 students in ECP, SCSE and GROW, and all projections assume 100 SOC kindergarten and 50 SOC first grade students. Schools of Choice enrollment ran 287 in Fall 2009/10, 416 in 2010/11, 590 in 2011/12, 700 in 2012/13, 821 in 2013/14 and 907 in 2014/15. K-5 moved from 5,230 in 1997/98 to 4,964 in 2004/05 and back to 5,398 in 2014/15, with 2019/20 outcomes of 5,468 high, 5,130 most likely and 4,798 low. Grades 6-8 stood at 2,811, projected to 3,193, 3,070 or 2,950; grades 9-12 stood at 4,100, projected to 4,441, 4,187 or 3,935. K-12 head count was 11,841 in 2000/01 and 11,955 in 2009/10, reaching 12,309 in 2014/15, projected to 13,102, 12,387 or 11,674 by 2019/20. Projected totals excluding SCSE/ECP/GROW run 12,227, 12,142, 12,055, 12,003 and 12,031 across 2015/16 to 2019/20, or 12,462, 12,377, 12,290, 12,238 and 12,226 including the 235. Comparisons show 2013/14 projected 12,494 against actual 12,573, and 2014/15 projected 12,653 against actual 12,556.

**Items 7.B and 7.C, curriculum reports.** Mrs. Haezebrouck reports on the three-year pilot of Reading Recovery, Kinder-Core and Teaching and Learning Leaders begun in 2013-2014. Reading Recovery teacher representatives are Natalie Haezebrouck, Heidi Palaj, Joni Gabriel and Trudy Motzenbecker; Teaching and Learning Leaders are Carol Machak, Kaity ORiordan and Shari Pawlus. Training of two Reading Recovery teachers serving Leonard and Wattles moves from weekly and year-long with four half days of Kinder-Core PD to monthly with LLI in kindergarten and two half days; the teacher lab expands to all third grade teachers, and a typical day serves four first graders. Other initiatives include Hamilton reading instruction for grades K-3 and work with 34 teachers bridging sixth grade general and special education math support. District Science Coordinator Jessica Ashley with biology teachers Andrea Bolterstein and Jennifer Sprague present "Biotechnology in OneTroy 2014-2015" on Technology Bond equipment including autoclaves, centrifuges, digital micropipettes, spectrophotometer, microscopes and MiniOne Systems, involving Richard Chan from The MiniOne System and roughly 1,000 freshmen biology students in pipetting, gel loading and PTC gene labs aligned to NGSS.

**Item 8.A, Smith Middle School and Niles School remodeling.** Bids were reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248.823.4050; Doug Madden of Barton Malow; and Michelle Kerns, Owners Representative. RFP Bid 9804 was issued February 16, 2015 for Smith gymnasium and locker room bleachers, electrical and lighting upgrades and painted finishes, and Niles restroom fixture and lighting replacement. Low bids awarded from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund are category 061000 General Trades to Advanced Building Group at $154,000.00, category 096400 Wood Flooring to Foster Specialty Floors at $41,940.00, category 126600 Telescopic Stands to Interkal at $22,546.00, category 230000 Mechanical to Contrast Mechanical at $21,700.00 and category 260000 Electrical to Metro Electric at $68,300.00, totaling $308,486.00. Competing bids included E&L Construction Group at $194,700.00, Heritage at $199,500.00, Construction Solutions at $211,700.00, Kiefer Specialty Flooring at $42,555.00 and Irwin Seating Company at $24,859.00; Advanced Building Group's alternate to paint locker interiors adds $16,300.00.

**Item 8.B, Data Storage and Backup Solution.** Kris Young, Director of Technology, John Foster of Convergent Technology Partners and Rick West recommend awarding the contract to EMC/Presidio for $469,750.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. The April 1, 2015 letter from Convergent Technology Partners, 801 S. Saginaw Suite 505, Flint, MI 48502, signed by John C. Foster, RCDD, President and Kristie Young, notes five years of maintenance and configuration for 5% growth over each of the next five years. The existing EMC system, purchased three years ago, carries approximately $345,000 due this year rising roughly 15% annually; the new system starts at approximately $50,000 per year in year six. VMAXe five-year cost totals $1,956,185 against XtremIO at $399,750 after a $150,000 trade-in on $549,750, a total cost of ownership of $1,556,435; backup maintenance totals $154,292 estimated against $90,000 proposed, a TCO of $64,292. Storage at $399,750.00 plus backup at $90,000.00 gives $489,750.00 less a $20,000.00 bundle discount. WSCA pricing on a $907,195.00 list gives $657,716.38 at 27.5% and $399,750.00 at a total 55% discount. XtremIO offers 20.00TB raw and 17.00TB useable capacity and up to 150,000 IOPS; the backup appliance is 24 TB with Data Domain DD Boost.

**Item 10.A, Bond Projects Update.** Barton Malow and TMP report on the 2013 Bond Program Series 1: Troy High School classroom and storage additions and Boulan Park and Larson office additions completing around December 2015, and the Athens LGI and multi-use classroom renovation in spring 2015. BP #8 Athens mechanical and electrical upgrades and BP #11 International Academy East pool-to-LGI conversion go out for bids August 2015; BP #9 Larson and Boulan mechanical, electrical and site paving bids were due April 7, 2015; BP #13 Smith and Niles contracts are awarded April 14, 2015.

**Items 10.B through 10.E, board policies.** First readings cover B-1210 Closed Session, which requires five affirmative roll call votes except for purposes 1, 2 and 3, lists seven permitted purposes, cites Section 10, 11 or 13 of Act No. 267, Public Acts 1976, destroys closed session minutes one year and one day after approval, and was adopted April 8, 1975 and revised March 15, 1977, March 17, 1998 and April 15, 2003; B-1301 Agenda Format, revised April 20, 2010; and B-1401 Minutes, requiring proposed minutes within eight business days and approved minutes within five, compliance with the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, Act No. 442, PA 1976, and official minutes bound in the vault at the administrative office, revised April 17, 2012. A separate first reading amends J-2012 Anti-Bullying Policy, adopted June 5, 2012 and revised May 6, 2014, for cyberbullying under Michigan Public Act 478 Revised School Code, referencing Section 219a of the Michigan Penal Code, 1931 PA 328, MCL 750.219a. Second readings and adoption cover B-0102 Board Members' Term of Office, setting six-year terms beginning with the November 2016 general school election and even years thereafter, adopted January 15, 2008; B-1202 Place of Meeting, adding twenty-four hours advance notice; B-1204 Quorum, setting four members as a quorum and permitting non-voting remote participation subject to the Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.261 et seq., revised July 10, 2012; and B-1211 Public Participation, limiting participation to 60 minutes per Board meeting in place of two 30-minute segments, requiring Speaker Request Forms available 30 minutes prior to the meeting, and allowing up to three minutes per speaker with no transfer of time.
